prompt: What is a service level indicator?

choices.text: The share of events that went well, measured where customers meet the service
A target the service has to meet over a month, written down and agreed with customers
The number of servers a service runs on
choices.why: Not a measure of what customers get.

choices.text: A contract with a penalty for missing it, signed with each large customer of the service

prompt: Why does the shop's availability SLI count a `402`, a declined card, as a good event?

choices.text: Because 4xx codes are too rare to matter
choices.why: 75 in five minutes is not rare.

choices.text: Because the storefront cannot tell a 402 from a 201
The system worked: the card network said no and the customer was told
Because declined cards are retried by the storefront until one of the attempts succeeds

prompt: A latency SLI wants the share of checkouts under 300 ms, but the histogram's buckets are 250 ms and 500 ms. What follows?
hint: A histogram answers for its boundaries.

choices.text: Prometheus interpolates the 300 ms share exactly
The SLI should use the average instead
choices.why: An average hides the slow ones.

choices.text: The threshold can be any number, since Prometheus estimates the share between two buckets exactly
A 300 ms bucket has to be added, or a threshold of 250 or 500 chosen

prompt: Why should an SLI name the route a customer uses rather than count every route?
hint: What else answers on a service.

choices.text: Prometheus cannot sum over routes
Probes and other traffic would count as satisfied customers
Every route has its own objective, required by the regulator for online shops
Counting every route is slower to compute, and the rule would time out at each evaluation

prompt: Why is 100% the wrong objective?

choices.text: Because Prometheus cannot store the number 1
Because no customer cares about reliability
Customers cannot tell it from 99.99%, and it forbids every change
Because 100% costs exactly twice as much as 99%, in servers and in people on call

prompt: How many minutes of total outage does a 99.9% objective allow in 28 days? Answer to the nearest minute.
Why is 28 days a common SLO window rather than a calendar month?

choices.text: It always holds four of each weekday
Because Prometheus keeps exactly 28 days of data
Because months are too long for any team to remember an incident
Because contracts require it

prompt: How should an SLA relate to the SLO for the same service?

choices.text: It should be stricter, to impress customers and win contracts against rivals
choices.why: The team would miss it first.

choices.text: It should be identical, so that customers and the team read one number
choices.why: Then trouble reaches the contract with no warning.

choices.text: It should not exist if there is an SLO
It should be looser, so the SLO warns before the contract is broken

prompt: At 99.5% over a window with 1 000 000 checkouts, how many may fail?
What does the error budget turn the objective into?

choices.text: A penalty paid to customers
An allowance of failures, to be spent on change and risk
A limit on how many releases a month are allowed, agreed with the product team
A count of incidents written in the postmortem

prompt: Over a window, the SLI is 99.8% and the objective 99.5%. What fraction of the budget is left?

choices.why: That is the difference of the two, not the budget left.

prompt: Prometheus rules that store the result of an expression as a new series are called ___ rules.
hint: The field each rule starts with.

prompt: Why write the SLI as recording rules rather than as a query in each dashboard?

choices.text: Recording rules are the only way to compute a ratio
Dashboards cannot read from Prometheus directly
Dashboards and alerts read the same numbers from one definition
Recording rules keep their data for longer than raw series, so a 28-day window fits

prompt: Why does the lab use a one-hour window instead of 28 days?

choices.text: Because Prometheus refuses windows longer than a day
Because one hour is the recommended window for production
Because the lab's disks cannot hold 28 days of samples
So that a lesson sees it move; the expressions are the same

prompt: During the incident, checkouts fail at 5% against an allowed 0.5%. What is the burn rate?
Why can one short incident spend a large share of a one-hour budget but a small share of a 28-day one?
hint: The budget grows with the window.

choices.text: A 28-day window forgets incidents after a day
Failures are counted only once a day in a long window
choices.why: They are counted as they happen.

choices.text: The same failures are measured against far more allowed failures
The objective is looser over 28 days

prompt: What makes an error budget policy work?

choices.text: It is agreed in advance and applied by the number, not by debate
A meeting to decide each freeze when the budget is low, chaired by the most senior engineer
choices.why: A debate each time is what it avoids.

choices.text: Naming who spent the budget
choices.why: It is about pace, not people.

choices.text: It is kept secret from the feature teams
choices.why: They have to agree to it.

prompt: A team's budget has never been spent in a year. What does the section suggest?

choices.text: Celebrate, and leave everything as it is
Lower the objective to 99% so the budget gets used and the numbers look normal
Stop measuring the SLI, since a value that never changes tells the team nothing
Release faster or tighten the objective until it means something

prompt: A load test runs against production for an hour and every request succeeds. What happens to the SLI if it counts all traffic?
hint: Good events that are not customers.

choices.text: It falls, because tests are counted as failures
It rises, hiding failures real customers had
It stays the same, since Prometheus ignores tests
It becomes undefined

prompt: Checkouts are 99.7% available over 28 days, the objective is 99.5%, and customers complain loudly about failed payments. What is wrong?

choices.text: The SLI or the objective: it does not match what customers feel
The customers, since the objective is met
The window should be shortened to one hour
choices.why: That changes nothing about what is counted.

choices.text: Prometheus is losing samples

prompt: Put the steps of setting up an SLO in order.
hint: Measure, then target, then agree what happens.
items: Choose the event customers care about and how to count it
Record the SLI and look at its history
Set the objective and the window
Alert on how fast the budget burns
